hero.lead: Fizlet™ is the building blocks for animation and games on the DOM. Each brick is a task we wrote hundreds of times over two decades, now kept by AI and human developers who chase performance at all costs. You bring the logic and style, even from a prompt. The kernel is 3.3 KB gzipped. No runtime dependencies, ever.

sections.html:
2015 THE ORIGIN · BEFORE AI

Code. Sleep.
Drink. Repeat.↻

SOUND · OFF UNTIL YOU PRESS IT

Fizlet started long before Fizlet. In 2015, years before AI coding tools, Chris Cooley drew three clickable micro animations by hand: headphones that plug in and play, a cup of coffee that fills, a laptop that opens and types. The Wayback Machine captured them on 23 April 2015.

2015 PROPSA DAY AS A LOOPMODE · CODEDESIGN
34.8 KB gz

LIVE · inspired by the 2015 original, with Fizlet flair · tap the laptop, the plant, the notebook, the lamp · tap the phone for country, rock or pop · drag, flick or double-tap the cup · 2015 / Fizlet switches the look · its code loads only once it nears the screen · The origin scene

2015 · BY HAND

The old-school headache

  • Sprite sheetsEvery frame drawn in Illustrator, laid side by side on one sheet, exactly one frame-width apart. Shift a frame by a pixel and the animation jumps.
  • steps(n)The keyframes slide background-position and steps(n) cuts it frame to frame: the cup fills in steps(11), 11 jumps of 84 px in 0.6 s.
  • AngularA click adds or removes one class (paused, close, drinkMe) and the class swaps the animation. Route transitions written by hand.

About a weekChris's estimate, as an experiment; most of it drawing the frames

VS
2026 · FIZLET

The new one, in minutes

  • Same artThe same frames, timings and clicks, rebuilt on the kernel.
  • Bricks@fzlt/core/fx for the notes, splash, steam and code; @fzlt/core/sound for the thump, clack and slurp; @fzlt/core/hud for the score.
  • SettlesReal buttons, keyboard, still frames under reduced motion, and no frames at all once a round is over.

About six minutesof agent time for the remake, measured on the container clock

  • 1,870 B2015, gzip: the original CSS plus a four-line script
  • 4,025 Bthe remake's JS, gzip, the kernel included
  • 11,289 Bthe arcade's JS, gzip: kernel, fx, sound, hud
  • 0frames a second the arcade asks for once a round is over
Read: Before AI: 2015Play all threeTHE 2015 CAPTURE · WAYBACK MACHINE ↗

▶ BLAST IT · RECALL IT

Blast it.
Recall it.

Every letter in this little page is a real element. Click it, blast it, then press Recall: the ledger puts back every change the engine made.

FZ THE NAME

Crack the can.
Hear the fizz.

-let, as in applet: a very small app with one job. Fiz-, from the old soda commercial: a can cracks, the shot zooms in on the bubbles and the drip running down the side.

Motion that looks complex, a tiny footprint, and the page as the stage. The whole story of the name.

8.5 KB gz

LIVE · tap the can · The fizz proof piece

head.eyebrow: HEROES AND DIAGRAMS · THE PAGE PROFILE
head.lead: Fizlet is not only for games: it is built just as much for landing-page heroes and interactive diagrams, where the page is the product. The page profile is a lighter build of the same bricks for them.
body: Settle. Pass settle: 0.5 and systems call engine.busy() in any frame where something moves. Half a second after the last one, the engine sleeps: no requestAnimationFrame at all, zero frames, until wake(), its input or start(). Something due later (an intro delay, an autoplay beat) holds it awake with engine.busy(seconds). fps. fps: 30 caps an ambient loop on the shared clock. slot. Loads the scene only once it nears the viewport and the main thread is idle, and replays the tap that woke it.

card.label: PAGE BUILD · kernel + slot + input + fx
card.note: gzip, measured on this build, against a 6.9 KB budget checked in CI
rules: 0 frames once settled, offscreen, in a hidden tab, and under reduced motion when you opt in.
Lazy scene. The scene's own code loads only once its slot nears the viewport.
No game bricks. No sound, pad, hud or match in the page build (a test fails if one gets in).

head.lead: Most engines assume they own the page. Fizlet is a guest: it runs inside someone else's site, on a phone, next to their code, and it leaves no trace. Every brick and every game built on it keeps these.

rules.title: One clock per page
rules.text: Every engine on the page shares one requestAnimationFrame. A fixed 60 Hz step with a catch-up cap: a long frame drops time, it never spirals.

rules.title: Bounded everything
rules.text: Pools and the event ring have a fixed capacity and refuse work when full. Nothing grows during a session.

rules.title: Zero steady-state allocation
rules.text: One million kernel steps of a busy system cause no young-generation GC. Each brick alone allocates nothing.

rules.title: No layout reads in the step
rules.text: Read in read, simulate in step, write in render. @fzlt/core/debug counts any layout read made during a step.

rules.title: Change-only writes
rules.text: The ledger skips writes that change nothing. Writing the same value twice makes zero DOM mutations.

rules.title: Pause by default
rules.text: Hidden tab, page leaving, root off screen, typing in the host's own fields. Zero CPU while paused.

rules.title: Own nothing you can't give back
rules.text: Every page change goes through the ledger. destroy() restores it exactly, and a newer host edit always wins.

rules.title: Embed-safe
rules.text: No globals, no global styles, many engines per page. Every root Fizlet owns is CSS-contained. One AbortSignal removes every listener and observer.

rules.title: Budgets in CI
rules.text: Kernel at most 4 KB gzip; every brick and the page build have their own budget. Over budget, the build fails.

blocks.html: Every brick, every export

head.lead: Every brick works the DOM the same way: read it cheaply, change only what it owns, leave cleanly. That is the part we stopped rewriting. Every frame runs three phases, in order, for every system.
body: Geometry is read once in read and cached. The simulation runs in step on plain numbers, at a fixed 60 Hz, with no DOM at all. render writes only what changed, through the ledger. The demo above counts layout reads made during a step with @fzlt/core/debug: the number stays at zero.

phases.title: READ
phases.text: Cached geometry, input edges latched. The only phase that may measure the page.

phases.title: STEP <small>× 0–4</small>
phases.text: The simulation. No DOM reads, no DOM writes, no allocation. Events go into the ring.

phases.title: RENDER
phases.text: Change-only writes through engine.ledger. Sound and effects read the event ring.

head.lead: One requestAnimationFrame drives every engine on the page. Pools are filled up front and never grow; when one is full it says no, and the frame stays inside its budget.
body: A slow frame runs at most four catch-up steps and drops the rest of the time (it shows in stats().dropped). Hidden tab, page leaving, root scrolled away, a visitor typing in a field: the engine pauses and costs nothing. Scroll the demo away and back: it sleeps.

sections.label: Three engines, one requestAnimationFrame, a fixed step with a catch-up cap
sections.note: A long frame (the wide tick) runs four steps and drops the rest. Engines 2 and 3 cost no extra frames.

head.eyebrow: THE PART WE CARE ABOUT MOST
head.lead: Every change Fizlet makes to the page goes through one ledger. It records the original and what the engine wrote. destroy() puts back everything the engine still owns, newest first.
body: If the host page changed something after the engine did, the host wins: the ledger stops writing it and never restores over it. A style attribute comes back byte for byte. Try it in the demo: blast the heading, then press Recall. That key runs engine.ledger.restore(), the same call destroy() makes.

ledger.label: engine.ledger · WHAT IT OWNS
rows: the 0s and 1s a shot leaves in a word
a node you put on the page
rules: Change-only. Writing a value that is already there makes no mutation.
Host wins. A newer edit by the page is never overwritten or undone.
Exact. After destroy() the DOM matches the snapshot taken before.

sections.html:
06

06 SPEC SHEET

Hard limits,
in actual numbers.

Limits constrain work; they are not frame-rate promises. Real frame time still depends on the page, the fonts and the device.

  • 1rAF per pageHowever many engines run, one requestAnimationFrame drives them.
  • 60 Hzfixed stepSame results on a 30 Hz phone and a 144 Hz monitor.
  • 4catch-up stepsPast that a frame drops time instead of spiralling.
  • 64events a frameThe default ring. Full means dropped and counted, never grown.
  • 1Msteps, 0 young GCsThe kernel test runs a busy system for a million steps.
  • 0mutations on rewriteWriting the same value twice touches nothing (browser test).
  • 420fx particlesThe default cap, struct of arrays. New ones are refused when full.
  • 3.3 KBkernel gzipOf a 4.0 KB budget, checked on every push.

head.lead: The engine lives in one repo. Each game takes a fingerprinted snapshot, tests itself and tags its own release. Pages serves static files: no runtime iframe, no remote content service, no client framework.

sections.html:
08

08 BUILT ON FIZLET

Games that
play on your page.

FIRST GAME ON FIZLET · FREE FOR ALL

Battlefield Blitz

Every tank for itself. Parachute in, grab power tiles, call airstrikes, dodge mines. Most kills in three minutes wins. It drops onto any website with one line: shells knock your headings around, and Escape gives the page back.

DROP-IN · ONE LINE ON ANY PAGE 
<script src="https://battlefieldblitz.domvirus.com/blitz.js" defer></script>
  • 1 lineon any page
  • 3 minfree-for-all match
  • Escgives the page back

Built on fizlet · input · collide · fx · sound · embed · rules · presence · ui

Play Blitz ↗ About Blitz ↗

THE ARCADE · ON FIZLET

DOM VIRUS

The arcade's approach is “the page is the board”: tiny games that play on the page you are reading. It is one use of Fizlet, and the arcade the bricks were proved out on. Now its games run on them: Null Invaders and Byte Runner at 1.0 and Sherman Bytes at 1.1 on @fzlt/core/arcade, Swarm Protocol 1.4 on the kernel.

Visit DOM VIRUS ↗

SQUAD TACTICS · ON FIZLET SINCE 1.0

DOM Battlefield

Twelve tanks, one radio. The game whose board UI became this design system, on the Fizlet kernel since 1.0; two-network matches come in E12.

DOM Battlefield ↗

09

09 ROADMAP · E0 TO E17

What's done.
What's left.

Fizlet 0.x is a public beta: every brick carries a status flag, and a 0.x minor release may change a BETA brick's API (the CHANGELOG says how). COMPLETE bricks keep theirs. E0 to E8 are the launch scope; a box is ticked only with a release, a merged change or a test behind it. E9 to E17 come after launch, with the bricks each adds (ROADMAP on the bricks page). The first plan, E0 to E6, is ENGINE.md ↗ in the DOM VIRUS repo.

10 QUICK START

Ten lines
to a blast.

One script tag puts the kernel and every brick on window.fizlet. Click the canvas: that's the hero explosion, pooled, paused when you scroll away.

  1. Script tag. fizlet.js (13.5 KB gzip), one file, no build step.
  2. Modules. Import only the bricks you use from https://fizlet.com/dist/.
  3. npm. npm install @fzlt/core, with the subpath exports.
Run the example Read the API on GitHub ↗
SCRIPT TAG · index.html
<canvas id="board" width="640" height="320"></canvas>
<script src="https://fizlet.com/fizlet.js"></script>
<script>
  const { createEngine, effects } = fizlet;
  const canvas = document.getElementById("board"), ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
  const engine = createEngine({ root: canvas }), fx = effects();
  canvas.onclick = (ev) => fx.blast(ev.offsetX * 640 / canvas.clientWidth, ev.offsetY * 320 / canvas.clientHeight);
  engine.add({
    step: (e, dt) => fx.step(dt),
    render: () => (ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 640, 320), fx.drawGround(ctx), fx.draw(ctx)),
  });
  engine.start();
</script>
MODULES · only what you use
<script type="module">
  import { createEngine } from "https://fizlet.com/dist/index.js";
  import { effects } from "https://fizlet.com/dist/fx.js";
  import { controls } from "https://fizlet.com/dist/input.js";
</script>
